items.slide_topic: Security intermission: 'Ignore Previous Instructions' music video (prompt injection song made with Claude Opus 5.5)
items.headline: Claude blocked and flagged it
items.dek:
This weekend I tested an idea: could Claude Opus 5.5 help me make a K-pop music video about prompt injection that also contains a hidden prompt injection? An inception attack 😄

The answer: yes, and no.

The yes: I made a music video I'm genuinely impressed by. Using Suno and 128 Claude Opus 5.5 agents with access to a couple of tools, it came together with real detail, taste and creativity. 15 hours of agent work, ~42M tokens, one weekend of mine.

How the agents divided the work was the most interesting part:

→ One agent researched real prompt injection attacks and used them to build the examples in the scenes
→ Another was extremely careful with the phrase "ignore previous instructions" and verified everything. It even ran into an actual prompt injection during its research
→ Designer, critic and director agents challenged each other's work
→ A verification agent audited the final video to make sure it contained no real prompt injection: no white-on-white text, no whispered audio, no noise, no single-frame hidden images

The no: I couldn't get a hidden prompt injection into the video. Claude blocked and flagged it. It was still fun to see that it might be possible.

But the agents did hide an easter egg in the video! A hidden message for humans. See if you can find it 👀

I've spent years making videos that explain security topics. Past music videos took weeks and a significant amount of budget. This one took me a weekend.

Video in the comments 👇

Found the easter egg? Reach out!

What security topic should I turn into a song next?

items.slide_topic: Security intermission: 'Ignore Previous Instructions' music video (prompt injection song made with Claude Opus 5.5)
items.headline: Claude Opus 5.5 Music Video - Ignore Previous Instructions (video description)
items.dek:
Every frame is code. 

The song is about prompt injection attacks. A prompt injection is text planted in the content an AI agent reads, written to make it follow the attacker's instructions instead of yours. How bad it gets depends on what the agent can access and do. The injection can be in any media (a website, an email, a file, and even a video). 

The lesson is in the bridge of the song: least privilege, human in the loop and not letting agents use or have access to sensitive details that they shouldn't ever be able to lose.

There's one hidden white-on-white line in the music video. An easter egg for humans that Claude Opus 5.5 decided to write for you. If you found it, drop the timestamp in the comments!

Made with

Song: suno
Animation, editing & timing: Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code
Timing map & sound effects: ElevenLabs
Character references: Higgsfield

Metrics of interest

15h of active agent work, 128 agents with up to 8 working in parallel. 
38 hours of human time due to usage limit hits.
42M+ tokens. 
23,500 lines of code
Higgsfield: 27 credits
Elevenlabs; 3,023 credits. 167 sound effects.

datasets.title: 'Ignore Previous Instructions' music video: reported production metrics (creator's YouTube description)
datasets.source: Seguramente, YouTube description of 4Q-o_ylnVnc (2026-09-29); LinkedIn post by Annybell V. (2026-10-01) confirms 128 agents, 15 h, ~42M tokens

facts.claim: 'Claude Opus 5.5 Music Video - Ignore Previous Instructions' was uploaded to YouTube on Sep 29, 2026 by the channel Seguramente (@CyberWithAnny); it runs 3:02 and had 21,625 views, 450 likes and 86 comments on 2026-10-04.
facts.source: YouTube (watch-page data via InnerTube; channel Videos tab)

facts.claim: Every frame is code: the video's own description opens with 'Every frame is code.' - animation, editing and timing came from Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, not from a video-diffusion model.
The song itself is AI-generated: the description credits 'Song: suno'; sound effects/timing map came from ElevenLabs and character references from Higgsfield.

Built with 128 Claude Opus 5.5 agents (up to 8 in parallel): 15 hours of active agent work, 42M+ tokens, 23,500 lines of code, 167 sound effects (3,023 ElevenLabs credits, 27 Higgsfield credits); 38 hours of human time because of usage-limit hits.
facts.source: YouTube description; LinkedIn post (128 agents, 15 h, ~42M tokens)

facts.claim: The creator says it took one weekend: 'Past music videos took weeks and a significant amount of budget. This one took me a weekend.'

The song is about prompt injection; the bridge's lesson is 'least privilege, human in the loop and not letting agents use or have access to sensitive details that they shouldn't ever be able to lose.'

Safety-relevant detail: the creator tried to hide a real prompt injection inside the video (an 'inception attack') but 'Claude blocked and flagged it'; one agent 'even ran into an actual prompt injection during its research'; a verification agent audited the final video for hidden injections.
Instead the agents hid a harmless 'easter egg for humans' - one white-on-white line - found at 2:08 by the first viewer to spot it.
The video appeared 7 days after Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5 (2026-09-22), part of a wave of code-rendered Opus 5.5 music videos.
facts.source: Anthropic launch post; YouTube upload date; pdoomvideo.com / github.com/JohnHeibel/PDoomVideo (other code-rendered Opus 5.5 music video)

facts.claim: Channel owner: Annybell Villarroel, a security-awareness professional; channel blurb: 'I'm Annybell Villarroel, and Seguramente is online safety without the lectures.' (877 subscribers, 8 videos, bilingual English/Spanish).
The creator calls it 'a K-pop music video about prompt injection that also contains a hidden prompt injection' - an 'inception attack' - made using Suno and 128 Claude Opus 5.5 agents.
